decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts build directly on the firm's glass structuring, drilling and bonding know-how, so its own R&D can keep refining them for MEMS packaging customers.
Carrier wafers for smaller diameters are a close extension of the established carrier and thin-wafer handling business and fit the strategic push toward reusable carriers at low cost.

The Cu-interposer glass wafer is a flagship advanced-packaging technology that builds on the firm's through-glass via and metallization expertise, and its R&D and EU project experience help it learn from early customer qualification.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand repackages the firm's core glass and quartz wafer competence into a standard product line, a low-risk channel that fits its existing knowledge base.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core wafer business and the firm has limited related knowledge to interpret results, but they share the through-glass via and metallization technology with the interposer, so the firm keeps them for now while the risk of dropping them stays high.
